per_option_rationale.rationale: When expanding -3(x-1), the student writes -3x - 3 instead of -3x + 3, dropping the sign on the constant term: 4x+10-3x-3 = 24 gives x + 7 = 24, x = 17.
The student correctly reaches x + 13 = 24 but then computes 24 - 13 = 12 instead of 11, a one-unit arithmetic slip in the final subtraction.

When multiplying through by 6, the student distributes 2 to 2x but not to the constant 5, writing 2(2x+5) as 4x+5 instead of 4x+10. This is an order-of-operations error: multiplication is not applied to all terms in the bracket. The equation becomes 4x+5-3x+3 = 24, giving x + 8 = 24, x = 16.

explanation: Multiply every term by LCM(3,2) = 6: 2(2x+5) - 3(x-1) = 24. Expand carefully: 4x+10-3x+3 = 24. Collect: x + 13 = 24. Solve: x = 11.

explanation_sections.punchline: x = 11. The decisive transformation is clearing all fractions in one step by multiplying through by LCM(3, 2) = 6. After that it is straight linear algebra. The killer trap is expanding -3(x - 1) as -3x - 3 instead of -3x + 3, which shifts the answer to 17.
explanation_sections.approach: Transformation plan: (1) find LCM of all denominators (here 6), (2) multiply every term - including the integer RHS - by 6, (3) expand every bracket carefully, writing each sign change explicitly, (4) collect x-terms left and constants right, (5) solve. Write the expansion line out in full even if it feels slow - sign errors on bracketed negatives are the single most common error on this question type.
explanation_sections.lesson: -3(x - 1) = -3x + 3. The minus outside distributes to every term inside, flipping the sign of the constant. Doing this step mentally is how 17 appears.
explanation_sections.timing: About 75 seconds. Clearing fractions in 15 seconds, expanding and collecting in 30 seconds, solving in 5 seconds. Back-substitute x = 11: (27/3) - (10/2) = 9 - 5 = 4. Verification takes under 15 seconds.
